text:
jess (AE): Heads-up — Sentinel just sent over a list of blockers for the migration POC. main asks: prompt parity, streaming diffs, and their security questionnaire. can we triage?

eli (SE): ok — can you paste the questionnaire and the sample requests they said cause diffs?

jess (AE): pasted below (redacted). they compared calls to CompetitorX and got different token counts + slightly different completions. also worried about our streaming chunk sizes breaking their client.

maria (security): send the questionnaire. quick note: they require SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for key‑wrap, VPC peering or dedicated private deployment, and 13 months of audit logs retention.

jess (AE): here's the redacted snippet of their sample call and expected output from CompetitorX:
```
POST https://api.competitorx.ai/v1/generate
{ "prompt": "Summarize the following note:\n\n- user: I loved the new feature...", "max_tokens": 150 }
// response truncated
{ "text": "Short summary...", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 12, "completion_tokens": 45 }}
```
They say when they hit Redwood our completion_tokens is higher and the output wording drifts.

eli (SE): two quick thoughts: (1) tokenization differences are expected — we use byte-pair variants and different whitespace handling; we can provide token-level mapping and a shim to normalize counts for billing comparisons. (2) output drift could be model/version mismatch or temperature/default param differences. ask them which model alias they were using.

samir (infra): streaming: CompetitorX emits smaller chunks; our runtime batches and may emit bigger frames. we have a streaming toggle to favor lower-latency small-chunk streaming (tradeoff: slightly higher cost). i can enable it for the POC cluster.

jess (AE): they asked about dedicated capacity during POC so they can validate latency at scale — price sensitivity here. what's the minimum reserved config we can offer for a short trial and an add-on for burst?

eli (SE): propose a small Dedicated pool: 1 x A10G equiv reserve with autoscale burst to 2 nodes for short periods. estimate: $X/day (ballpark). also offer token billing parity: we can meter tokens with a conversion factor and show both raw and normalized counts in the Console.

maria (security): questionnaire Qs answered in brief: SOC2 in flight (report available by EOD Wed), KMS: we support AWS KMS and customer-managed CMEK for Private deployment, VPC peering + IP allowlist supported, SSO via SAML/OIDC. I need the completed doc to fill vendor contact fields.

jess (AE): i'll attach the doc here after this thread.

eli (SE): for prompt parity, i'll create a small adapter shim they can run client-side to map CompetitorX request envelope to Redwood API. sample mapping (quick):
```
# CompetitorX -> Redwood shim (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-mini","input":"Summarize the following note:\n\n- user: I loved the new feature...","max_output_tokens":150}'
```
This will also let us instrument token counts before/after.

samir (infra): action: i need the sentinel staging IPs and the list of endpoints they hit so we can pre-provision allowlist and set up routing for VPC peering.

jess (AE): sending IPs in DM. timeline note: they want a demo next Tue and a 2-week POC starting the following Mon if demo goes well.

maria (security): blocker: legal wants to confirm data residency for EU customers. do we have EU private deployment availability in their region?

eli (SE): yes — we have EU regions and can offer Private deployment in a partner DC if required. provide me their target region and we can scope infra effort.

jess (AE): another blocker from procurement: they want a reduction in token unit price if they commit to a 3‑month reserved plan for the POC. can we do a short-term commitment discount?

eli (SE): we can offer a POC promo: 25% off for a 3‑month reserved commit, or a usage cap with credits. finance needs a note but should be doable for strategic deals.

maria (security): i'll draft the security answers and attach the SOC2 artifact. also need a point of contact for penetration test coordination — who owns that?

samir (infra): i'll be the infra contact for pentest coordination. we should confirm the attack windows and the scope against the POC environment only.

jess (AE): great. next steps: eli to produce adapter shim + token mapping doc by EOD Fri, samir to confirm VPC/IP pre-provisioning and streaming toggle, maria to fill and return security questionnaire, jess to push pricing proposal and demo invite.

eli (SE): noted — will also prepare a short eval harness with their prompt set so they can compare outputs side-by-side.

infra-bot: Deployed temporary POC cluster (poc-sentinel-01) in us-east-1. streaming_low_latency=true.

jess (AE): :thumbsup: thanks team — i'll update Sentinel and loop back once demo is scheduled.

eli (SE): FYI — if we see consistent output deltas after parity config, we should propose a small finetune/eval step or deterministic temperature/pen settings to match wording.

jess (AE): added as optional line item in the proposal. done.
